scenario.summary: Attackers exploit a critical unauthenticated RCE in Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) affecting Atlassian Confluence and N-able N-central to gain initial footprints. Using AI-assisted automation, they harvest credentials from local databases and file attachments before pivoting to internal identity services and production cloud environments.

hunt.name: Axis RCE and Confluence Credential Harvesting
hunt.description: The adversary exploits a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Apache Axis. This hunt identifies the attack using a gated flow. The hunt first searches for HTTP 500 errors on the Axis SOAP endpoint. If potential exploit traffic is found, the hunt fans out to identify anomalous child processes spawned by the Java application, rare access to the Confluence attachment directory, and connections to known tunneling services. This approach allows an analyst to confirm the initial exploit, the execution of automated shells, and the subsequent harvesting of sensitive documents.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_path, status_code, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{vulnerable_uris}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_path) || ',') > 0 AND status_code = 500 AND http_method = 'POST' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify potential Axis exploitation by finding HTTP POST requests to the SOAP endpoint that resulted in an Internal Server Error (500), matching the behavior observed in successful compromises.
config.expected_signal: Rows naming hosts that received suspicious POST requests to the Axis endpoint. Silence suggests no active targeting of the SOAP API in the window.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%java%' AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%bash%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%sh%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%curl%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify Confluence's Java process spawning bash or network utilities, which indicates successful remote code execution from the Axis exploit.
config.expected_signal: A shell or curl process running under the confluence service account with a Java parent. This is a high-confidence indicator of exploitation.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, LOWER(process_name) AS proc, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE file_path LIKE '%/attachments/v4/%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY proc HAVING hosts <= 3
config.description: Identify rare processes accessing the Confluence attachment directory, revealing the automated data harvesting observed in the report.
config.expected_signal: Rare processes interacting with the attachment store. Normal web server activity should appear across the fleet; attacker scripts will be rare.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS lookups FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{tunnel_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.trycloudflare.com' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.pinggy.net') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name

config.expected_signal: Hosts resolving tunnel provider subdomains. This corroborates C2 activity following a successful exploit.
